resources.string: Wingmirror is a fork of AARE by prototux and its contributors, the open-source Android Auto replacement. The Android Auto protocol, the connection, the audio and nearly everything else here is their work; this fork adds the root screen cast mode. The people thanked below are AARE\'s. GPL-3.0-or-later, like AARE.
Every option of the cast, with or without root
Wingmirror shows this phone\'s screen on your car\'s screen. Pick the way that fits the phone; you can switch later.
The full cast: touch from the car, all sound in the car, the picture fitted to the car\'s screen, and nothing to confirm when you plug in.
Lite: the car shows the screen and plays media sound. You share the screen by hand each time; touch is simpler and some options aren\'t available.
Ready. Unlock the phone and plug it into the car.
Ready. Plug the phone into the car. Share the screen again next time.
The car shows the phone\'s screen, full screen. Unlock the phone and plug it in: nothing to confirm.
Everything: touch from the car, all sound, the display fitted to the car, no dialog on any connection.

For a phone that isn\'t rooted, or a quick try. The car sees the phone\'s screen and hears its media, and that is all: you share the screen by hand each time, and the switches that need root are greyed out below.
Tap before you connect, each time: Android asks to share the screen (choose the entire screen) and to let Wingmirror record what apps play. Android forgets it when the app stops.
Shared. Plug the phone into the car; it lasts until Wingmirror stops or you end the share.

Without root, touch from the car is slower and one finger only (see Touch from the car below), the phone\'s screen stays on and keeps its own shape (black bars on a wide car screen), only media sound reaches the car and the phone plays it too (turn the phone\'s volume down), apps that protect their screen show black, and there is no lock or unlock, hotspot or car GPS.

Without root, through an accessibility service: a tap, long press or swipe on the head unit is replayed on the phone when your finger lifts. One finger, no pinch; the car\'s Back and Home keys work, its other keys don\'t.

Tap to open Android\'s accessibility settings and turn Wingmirror on. If Android says the setting is restricted, open Wingmirror\'s app info first, tap the three dots and choose Allow restricted settings.
On. Touches on the car screen are replayed on the phone.
Without root: music and video sound only, through the screen share, on Android 10 or newer. Navigation voice, notifications and calls stay on the phone, and the phone keeps playing the media as well.
Without root the phone keeps its own GPS, unless you choose Wingmirror as the mock location app yourself in Android\'s Developer options.
Without root the phone\'s display can\'t be resized: the car shows it in its own shape and orientation. Turn the phone sideways for a wider picture.
Installed and on. It answers the car too, takes the same USB connection and makes every session drop within a second. Tap to open its page in Android\'s settings and choose Disable.
A system or Play Store update can turn it back on. Wingmirror checks when it starts, after a restart and as a car connects, and turns it off again.
The phone\'s screen isn\'t shared yet. Open Wingmirror on the phone, go to Screen cast and tap Share the screen.
Granted. Wingmirror mirrors the screen and sets its permissions itself, without Android\'s dialogs.
Tap to ask your root manager (Magisk, KernelSU, APatch). Choose to allow it for good: it is asked once.
Root was not granted. Allow Wingmirror in your root manager, then tap again.
Sending the phone\'s sound to the car through root needs Android 12 or newer: on this phone the cast has no sound.
Installed and on. It answers the car too, takes the same USB connection and makes every session drop within a second. Tap to turn it off on this phone (with root; nothing is uninstalled).
Turned off on this phone, so the car\'s connection is Wingmirror\'s alone.
Touches and keys on the head unit act on the phone, multi-touch included.
Switches the phone\'s panel off completely while connected. The phone stays awake behind it, so the cast keeps running.
Also dims the phone screen to nothing; what is left if this phone won\'t switch its panel off. Your brightness comes back when the car disconnects.
Every sound the phone makes goes to the head unit: music, video, games, navigation, notifications, alarms, ringtones. The phone itself stays quiet. Phone calls stay on the car\'s Bluetooth.
Locks the phone and turns its screen off as soon as the Android Auto session ends.
Wakes and unlocks the phone once the car has set up its Android Auto session, so the cast starts by itself.
A code is saved. Type a new one to replace it

Needed if the phone has a PIN or password: Wingmirror types it on the lock screen. It is stored encrypted on this phone only. Pattern locks can\'t be typed. After a restart, unlock the phone once by hand: Android won\'t run apps before that. Anyone who can start your car\'s Android Auto session then gets an unlocked phone.
Turns the phone\'s Wi-Fi hotspot on when the car connects and off when it disconnects. A hotspot that was already on is left alone. Android 11 or newer.

While connected, the phone\'s location comes from the car\'s GPS, not the phone\'s own receiver, for every app. Nothing to set up: root makes Wingmirror the mock location app. The car has to send its position; most do.
Holds the phone in the head unit\'s orientation, including apps that ask for portrait.
Resizes the phone\'s display to the shape of the car screen, so the picture fills it with no black bars.
The phone renders at the head unit\'s own resolution: pixel for pixel, and the lightest on the phone.
The phone renders as large as its own panel allows, in the head unit\'s shape, and the stream is scaled down for the car.
Your own size, in the head unit\'s orientation (width first).
Smaller fits more on the car screen: more map, more list. Goes below what Android\'s own Display size setting allows. At the smallest sizes some apps switch to their tablet layout.
Shrinks text on top of that, below Android\'s smallest font size. 100% leaves the phone\'s own setting alone. Both go back to normal when the car disconnects.
For a precise value instead of the sizes above: leave empty otherwise. Lower shows more, higher makes everything larger.
Wingmirror puts the display back when the car disconnects, and after a crash or reboot. This does it by hand.
Could not restore: root was not granted
Changes apply from the next connection.

When the car won\'t connect or the cast stops: tap this right after it happens. With root it saves why Android ended the app, what the phone\'s USB did and the related system log to %1$s. Nothing leaves the phone; the file is yours to share.
Could not save: root was not granted
Screen cast needs root. Open Wingmirror on the phone, go to Screen cast and grant root access.
Android refused to mirror the phone screen. The connection log in Wingmirror says why.
